extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: HELVIPAD is a real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation featuring 40K video frames from 29 video sequences across diverse indoor and outdoor environments with various lighting conditions. Collected using two 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a LiDAR sensor, it includes accurate depth and disparity labels by projecting 3D point clouds onto equirectangular images, along with an augmented training set with increased label density via depth completion.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two omnidirectional cameras (Ricoh Theta V 360°) in a vertical arrangement with a 19.1 cm baseline, capturing equirectangular images at 30 fps, paired with a synchronized Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor operating at 10 fps, mounted on a remotely controlled robot chassis. Data was collected across 29 video sequences in indoor and outdoor scenes on a university campus under diverse weather and lighting conditions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Depth completion techniques were applied to increase label density; regions with high uncertainty were filtered and original labels were retained in ambiguous regions. Labels are not provided for pixels at object boundaries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Equirectangular images captured at 4K/UHD resolution (3840×1920 pixels) at 30 fps from two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras, and LiDAR point clouds from an Ouster OS1-64 sensor with 64 beams and 42.4° vertical field of view operating at 10 fps.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automated depth completion pipeline using LiDAR point cloud temporal aggregation, spherical grid interpolation, and KISS-ICP for odometry; no manual annotations used
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has an exponential decay in pixel percentage with increasing depth due to decreased LiDAR precision over longer distances. Depth completion increases density of low-range depth values (0-10m range), enriching representation of closer objects. Indoor sequences show more rapid decline in pixel percentage beyond 10 meters compared to outdoor scenes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may have limited generalization to underrepresented situations such as outdoor scenes at night. LiDAR precision decreases over longer distances, affecting depth label quality at range. The dataset is captured at a single university campus, which may limit diversity of environments.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support development of omnidirectional depth estimation models capable of navigating in human environments, with potential applications in real-time systems.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains recordings of pedestrians in indoor and outdoor scenes, with an average of 13.33 pedestrians in indoor sequences and 17.65 pedestrians in outdoor sequences.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, and benchmarking omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models. It is also suitable for assessing robustness of depth estimation methods to diverse lighting conditions and depth ranges.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset includes 26 video sequences captured between December 2023 and February 2024. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Missing depth values were filled using a depth completion pipeline that interpolates depth on spherical grid points via temporally aggregated LiDAR point clouds. A weighted average of k-nearest neighbors is used for interpolation, with filtering to exclude points with high uncertainty (relative weighted variance) or insufficient nearby measurements (out-of-distribution threshold).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Temporal aggregation of LiDAR point clouds: each frame's point cloud is aggregated with those from the four preceding and four succeeding frames (no movement assumption) to increase the number of valid depth points. Sky and ground regions were cropped from images. Depth completion increased labeled pixel ratio from 12% to 61%.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: LiDAR point clouds were projected onto 360° equirectangular images via optimized rotation and translation transformations (minimizing reprojection error using BFGS optimization). Points were converted to spherical coordinates and projected onto the equirectangular plane. Depth values were converted to spherical disparity in degrees. Grid points outside the LiDAR vertical field of view were filtered out.
